_comment: Narration pack for the Tsumiki demo (tools/narrate-run.mjs). Authored once; no model per video. Requirements are the ONLY numbers spoken (R1–R8). Every cue is one `text` string, so the subtitle IS the voice line. The counter climax carries pass AND fail variants keyed on the 'Finish the sub-tasks' step — a green run says the count dropped correctly; the broken-counter run explains the regression. `group` ties the variants so the road not taken is not warned about.

intro.text: This is Tsumiki, a small task tracker, and specboard's own demo. One test proves its eight requirements — watch the R chips at the top turn green as each one is proven.

outro.text: Eight requirements, one flow, every value read off the screen you just watched. Green only when proven.

cues.text: R1: adding a task. I type it, press Add, and it appears in the list with an added-just-now stamp.
R2: editing. Double-click the title, rename it, and the row updates — the stamp flips to edited.
R3: sub-tasks. A task that has them becomes a container with a progress ring instead of a checkbox. Adding one grows the ring by itself, from one of three to one of four.
R4: I complete the sub-tasks one at a time. Nobody ever clicks the parent.
R5 is the subtle one. This counter is the real work left — open sub-tasks, plus standalone tasks. Seven right now.
One sub-task done, and the count drops by exactly one.
The last sub-task done — the container completes itself, and the count drops by two, not three. A container is scaffolding, never a task. R4 and R5 hold.
The count is wrong. A finished container is still being counted as one item left — it shows five where it should show four. R5 is red, caught right on the screen.
And the other direction: reopening a sub-task reopens the parent — the ring drops back to three of four, and the count climbs to five.
R6: the smart views. For every view, the sidebar badge equals the rows you can actually see — I check each one.
R7: due dates. Against a frozen clock, the past-due task reads overdue, and the one due today reads today.
R8: a reload. The rename, the rolled-up ring, and every timestamp all come back — nothing lived only on screen.
